decisions.reason: The message's direct Lead Clipper changes are already captured by the candidate's same-message MODIFY; the quota variation-counting rule requires no additional change.
Treating hook variations as distinct production units does not change the requirement that clips receive client approval before counting or publication.
The variation-counting rule does not establish a new duration value; uncertainty from the separate shorter-style clause is already represented by the same-message AMBIGUOUS Event.
The new variation-counting rule does not change the submission channel, batch procedure, deadline, link delivery, or planned Notion workflow.
The source concerns ongoing approved-clip production and does not alter the qualification method, trial count, deadline, or success condition.
Reusing a body clip with different hooks does not change the permitted source materials or the existing source requirements for the current batch.
The ability to create hook variations does not remove or modify the requirement that each clip convey a complete standalone lesson, story, or point.
Changing a hook to create a variation does not alter the clean editing, effects, or transition standards.
The counting of clip variations toward production does not change which clips are authorized for publishing or any Instagram posting instructions.
The source permits hook variations but does not change caption color, font, effects, lettering, or position requirements.
The source discusses varying hooks and planned hook training, but it does not replace or modify the requirement to select strong source moments.
The clip-variation counting decision has no effect on the requirement to remove distracting wind noise.
